title: Quiz: Pollination and Fertilisation in Plants

options.text: The dispersal of seeds away from the parent plant
The fusion of male and female gametes
The germination of a seed into a plant
The transfer of pollen from an anther to a stigma

questions.explanation: Pollination is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther (male part) to the stigma (female part) of a flower. This can happen within the same flower (self-pollination) or between different flowers (cross-pollination).

questions.stem: What is the difference between self-pollination and cross-pollination?

options.text: Self-pollination produces seeds; cross-pollination does not
There is no difference between them
Self-pollination uses wind; cross-pollination uses insects
Self-pollination transfers pollen within the same flower; cross-pollination transfers it between different plants

questions.explanation: Self-pollination transfers pollen from anther to stigma within the same flower or plant. Cross-pollination transfers pollen between flowers on different plants of the same species. Cross-pollination produces more genetic variation.

questions.stem: What grows from the pollen grain after it lands on the stigma?
questions.explanation: After landing on a compatible stigma, the pollen grain germinates and grows a pollen tube. This tube grows down through the style to the ovary, carrying the male gamete to the egg cell inside the ovule for fertilisation.

questions.stem: Where does fertilisation occur in a flowering plant?

options.text: In the ovule inside the ovary

questions.explanation: Fertilisation occurs inside the ovule when the male gamete from the pollen tube fuses with the egg cell. The pollen tube enters the ovule through a tiny opening called the micropyle.

questions.stem: What does the ovule develop into after fertilisation?
questions.explanation: After fertilisation, the ovule develops into a seed. The fertilised egg cell inside the ovule develops into the embryo plant, and the ovule wall becomes the seed coat (testa) that protects the seed.

questions.stem: What does the ovary develop into after fertilisation?

options.text: The root of the new plant
The stem of the new plant

questions.explanation: After fertilisation, the ovary develops into a fruit. The fruit surrounds and protects the seeds and often aids in seed dispersal, for example by being attractive to animals or having structures for wind dispersal.

questions.stem: Why is cross-pollination generally considered advantageous over self-pollination?

options.text: It produces offspring with more genetic variation

questions.explanation: Cross-pollination transfers pollen between different plants, combining genetic material from two different individuals. This produces offspring with greater genetic variation, which improves the population's ability to adapt to changing conditions.
